open_points.subject: functions.issue_contract_version
open_points.text: State 4 says “the A02 rule 1 ceiling checks bind only a new version, so an equal one is returned even after a release lowered a ceiling below its bounds”; State 5 says “Purpose rule first (A01 rule 5); A02 rule 1 order; a bound above its ceiling or omitted is refused” without the equal-version exception.
open_points.question: After the purpose check, does resubmitting an existing equal contract version bypass the current release's A02 validation, particularly lowered ceilings?
options: Return the existing equal version before applying current release-dependent A02 checks
Revalidate every A02 condition and refuse an old equal version that is no longer valid
Bypass only ceiling checks but revalidate the other A02 conditions
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing equal version after the purpose and identity checks; apply current release validation only when creating a new version.

open_points.subject: runs.read_run
open_points.text: “The run's status, its WaitingPoints and its produced outputs are written by runs in its store calls” contradicts “Return a run's answer computed from its trace” and “Computed from the trace when asked, never stored”.
open_points.question: Which parts of a run answer are read from stored Run/WaitingPoint fields, and which are recomputed from the trace on every read?
options: Read stored status, waiting points and produced outputs; derive only missing-output reasons
Recompute the entire answer from trace records and ignore the stored copies
Recompute everything and repair any stored disagreement during the read
open_points.default_guess: Read the stored status, waiting points and produced outputs, and derive only each ended run's missing-output reason from the trace.

open_points.subject: map_index on mapped-node aggregate records
open_points.text: State 2 permits a mapped node to write a NodeExecution “with no map_index” when it maps an empty list or is skipped or upstream-failed before any element, while State 5 says “map_index is absent ... for an element of a node that is not mapped” and that absence “for one that is [mapped] is refused”.
open_points.question: How are the node-level NodeExecututions of mapped nodes identified and accepted by operations that name a NodeExecution?
options: Allow an absent map_index as a special aggregate record for a mapped node
Give aggregate records a distinguished sentinel index
Do not create aggregate records for mapped nodes
open_points.default_guess: Allow absent map_index for the expressly defined aggregate records, while requiring an index for element-targeting operations.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances
open_points.text: The operation rejects “an unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5)”, but A08 rule 5 mixes service-record checks, operation-specific checks, proposal-port checks and selected-instance checks, and startup names no operation or proposal ports.
open_points.question: Exactly which A08 checks and which capability entries must check_installed_instances validate at startup?
options: Validate only the service envelope and the selected instance facts needed for credential-header collision checks
Validate every capability entry using all checks that do not require proposal ports
Reject only unreadable JSON and otherwise inspect the selected instance's required headers
open_points.default_guess: Validate the service envelope and selected instance needed by the credential, but do not validate unrelated operation capabilities or checks requiring proposal ports.

open_points.subject: surface.serve_kernel MCP listener
open_points.text: The installation supplies “the mcp listen address”, but the fixed start sequence contains no validation or bind step for it, and serve_kernel specifies no outcome for a malformed address, an address already in use or another bind failure.
open_points.question: When is the MCP address parsed and bound, and how does a validation or bind failure affect recovery changes and process startup?
options: Validate during load_installation and bind after recovery immediately before opening the surface
Bind before store and recovery so address failure causes no recovery changes
Bind during load_installation as part of configuration loading
open_points.default_guess: Validate the address during installation loading, bind after successful recovery just before serving, and stop with a nonzero exit if binding fails; earlier committed recovery changes remain.

open_points.subject: unauthorized refusal response
open_points.text: Every refusal is required to carry “a bounded reason naming the first failing check”, while missing, unknown or revoked tokens and an invalid token list must receive “the same one refusal” that “reveals nothing”.
open_points.question: What reason, if any, accompanies unauthorized, and must it be byte-for-byte identical for all token-list and token-match failures?
options: Return one fixed generic reason for every unauthorized case
Return the unauthorized code with no reason
Name the specific failed token or configuration check
open_points.default_guess: Return one fixed generic reason, identical for all unauthorized cases.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution timestamps without execution or send
open_points.text: The convention defines started_at as “when the execution or send begins”, but NodeExecutions are also written for pre-send failures, owner refusals, skipped_by_guard, upstream_failed and empty mapped nodes, where neither an execution nor a send begins.
open_points.question: What exact instants populate started_at and ended_at for each NodeExecution that represents no execution or send?
options: Use the time its determining check or owner decision starts and the time its record is committed
Set started_at and ended_at to the same record-change time
Reuse an earlier related time such as approval requested_at
open_points.default_guess: Use the check or decision start for started_at and the record-change time for ended_at; use the same record-change time for both when there is no separately observable start.

open_points.subject: plain HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: Plain HTTP is allowed when the api_base_url “host is a loopback address”, without defining whether that means an IP literal, a hostname that resolves to loopback, or every address actually attempted by the connection.
open_points.question: How must service_invoker decide that a target is loopback, including localhost names, IPv6 and DNS answers?
options: Only a syntactically literal loopback IP address qualifies
A hostname qualifies when its current DNS answers are all loopback
A hostname qualifies when any selected connection address is loopback
open_points.default_guess: Only a parsed literal IPv4 or IPv6 loopback address qualifies.

open_points.subject: installation JSON parsing
open_points.text: load_installation requires “one JSON object with exactly the installation's fields” but does not say what happens when the JSON text repeats a member name.
open_points.question: Does a configuration object containing duplicate member names fail startup, or does a parser's first/last-value behavior apply?
options: Reject every duplicate member name
Keep the last occurrence
Keep the first occurrence
open_points.default_guess: Reject duplicate member names before schema validation.

open_points.subject: installation.resolve_service_credential
open_points.text: A credential file's content is decoded as UTF-8 “without one trailing newline”.
open_points.question: What byte sequence counts as the removable trailing newline, and is exactly one terminator removed when several are present?
options: Remove one final LF and also a preceding CR when it forms CRLF
Remove one final LF only, leaving any preceding CR to fail as a control character
Strip all trailing CR and LF characters
open_points.default_guess: Remove exactly one terminal line ending, treating LF and CRLF as one ending, and leave any additional trailing terminators to validation.

open_points.subject: store.put_value_bytes failures
open_points.text: put_value_bytes returns “refused when digest or size do not match”, but the global convention says a refusal is decided before the operation's first store change and writes nothing; callers can publish several values before a later put_value_bytes mismatch and none of their operation sections says whether this refusal is propagated or converted.
open_points.question: How must functions, flows, runs and effects handle a digest or size mismatch returned by put_value_bytes after earlier bytes may already have been published?
options: Treat it as an internal_error caused by a caller invariant defect
Propagate refused to the surface even if earlier unnamed bytes remain
Make publication of all bytes and their records one atomic store change
open_points.default_guess: Translate the mismatch to internal_error in the calling module; previously published unnamed bytes may remain under the existing orphan-byte rule.

open_points.subject: masked failure_detail length
open_points.text: A classified failure_detail is returned to an agent “only as its length and that class”.
open_points.question: Is the reported length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points or another unit?
options: UTF-8 byte length
Unicode code-point count
Character count after replacement and truncation as defined by the host language
open_points.default_guess: Report UTF-8 byte length, matching failure_detail_bytes_max.
